Gregory was planning a general Council of Arsenios the Latin Church at Lyons, in 1274, to discuss organizational matters and the new crusade. paragraphs.source_en: including Michael’s letter acknowledging the pope as supreme, with the au- thority to adjudicate all appeals within the Church; professing his passion for Union; and promising to enforce Union on any of his subjects who proved re- calcitrant. Prayers were chanted in both languages, including the filioque clause (three times). Union was formally proclaimed on 6 July, when the basileus’ pro- fession of faith (identical to that of Rome) was read to the Council, along with the concurring letter by the clergy of the eastern Church. There was no discussion or debate about the issues that divided the Churches. Akropolites, who had previ- ously written against Latin theology, took an oath in Michael’s name that he held to the faith of Rome, and more prayers were chanted (with the filioque, twice).
